newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks end higher, year-end rally continues.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks end higher, year-end rally continues.

text.p: Greek shares ended slightly higher on Tuesday with brokers expecting a year-end rally to last and a boost in volume due to active block trading.

"Tuesday's session was weak, with the exception of banks and construction firms which seem to perform better than other sectors. There is no power in the market, since people are cautious and do not show an investment interest," said Geli Petroulaki, broker at Ergasias Securities.

She said that trading volume increased over yesterday as a result of block trades, especially in Bank of Attica. The state Commercial Bank sold a 39.5 percent stake in Bank of Attica to two funds on Monday.

"I expect the general share index to fluctuate around 930 by end-year. In January, there might be some unrest following the announcement of audit results on securities companies. However, I do expect first new-year semester figures to bring prosperity back into the market," she added.
Several audits have been ordered by authorities of Athens brokerages following a 2.6 billion drachma fraud at Delta Securities which rocked the bourse in November.

"I consider today's session to have been particularly stabilising. This is a positive development, after the previous two sessions' decline of the general share index," said Iakovos Diamantopoulos of Kerdoos-Ermis Securities.
He expected the market share index to fluctuate around today's values until the end of December.
"I expect 1997 to be a good year, unlike 1996," he added.

The Athens general share index closed up 0.22 percent or 2.08 points at 933.12 from Monday's 931.04. It opened at 931.07. Trading volume rose to 29.5 billion drachmas on volume of 16.3 million shares in active block trading.
Gainers closely led losers 97 to 95 with 37 issues unchanged on 229 traded.
Banks gained 0.04 percent, construction rose 0.90 percent while small caps declined 0.64 percent and insurance shares dropped by 0.18 percent. Industrials closed 0.71 percent higher.
